contentBlocks.text: This week you moved from an atom's basic particles all the way to reading its full profile off the periodic table. Let's put every piece together on one new element.

Quick review: an atom's identity is set by its proton count, or atomic number (Day 1). Isotopes vary in neutron count; ions vary in electron count, but neither changes the element (Day 2). Electrons fill energy-level shells in order, and the outermost shell's electrons are valence electrons (Day 3). A period number matches the number of shells; a group number relates to the valence electron count (Day 4). Aluminum has atomic number 13 and mass number 27. Find its number of protons, neutrons, and electrons; determine its electron arrangement by shell; and state its number of valence electrons.

Excellent work this week — you can now read an atom's complete structure from just its position on the periodic table and a mass number. This foundation is essential for the unit on bonding coming up next.

objectives: Determine an atom's proton, neutron, and electron counts from its atomic and mass numbers
Determine an atom's electron arrangement by shell and its valence electron count
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child work through aluminum's full profile independently, using earlier days' worked examples as a model.
3. Complete the cumulative review worksheet.
4. Discuss any mismatches or uncertain answers together before finishing.
5. Celebrate finishing the first full week of this unit — this foundation carries directly into the bonding unit ahead.
differentiationTips: Struggling: allow the child to work through each sub-question (protons/neutrons/electrons, then shells, then valence) as separate steps rather than all at once
Ready for more: ask them to also predict whether aluminum would be more likely to lose or gain electrons to form an ion, based on its low valence electron count
This is a good checkpoint to note which part of the atomic-structure chain (basic particles, isotopes/ions, shells, or periodic table pattern) needs the most re-teaching
teacherGuide.answerKey: Aluminum (atomic number 13, mass number 27): 13 protons, 27-13=14 neutrons, 13 electrons (neutral). Electron arrangement: 2, 8, 3. Valence electrons: 3 (matches group 13).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates NGSS HS-PS1-1 (atomic structure and the periodic table's pattern of electron configurations) before the unit moves to bonding, matching the 'consolidate before adding more' pacing established across this session.

What is aluminum's electron arrangement by shell?
